cross_sector_overview: Across every sector, simultaneous structural transitions — SaH, NDIS, health digitisation, child protection, housing supply, and energy — are colliding with constrained fiscal headroom, creating acute demand for transition planning, governance assurance, and system redesign advisory work. Workforce instability and capability gaps are a consistent second-order pressure, while the Medicare AI hack and Snowy Hydro disclosure signal that cyber resilience and capital project transparency are emerging as standalone advisory priorities in their own right.

pepi_wide.brief: The 1 October 2026 Support at Home commencement has immediately generated Senate inquiry findings characterising the program as 'immoral' and rationing care, exposing a material gap between policy intent and delivery reality that signals near-term redesign procurement across KPMG's aged care advisory, financial modelling, and provider viability practices. Simultaneously, an AI-attributed breach of the Medicare portal has triggered an Auditor-General review and Prime Ministerial response, and the imminent digital duty of care framework signals a tightening compliance and assurance environment directly relevant to KPMG's health, digital, and risk advisory lines. Structural reform pressure is compounding across child protection (WA crisis point, royal commission risk), NDIS (three concurrent transition waves with Queensland yet to execute the Thriving Kids agreement), and education (Coalition curriculum reform platform), all pointing to state and federal procurement activity contingent on political and electoral dynamics. The fiscal backdrop is hardening: Labor is tracking toward a record tax-to-GDP ratio while Chalmers announces a $6b spend boost against 15-year-high interest rates, a combination that will intensify agency efficiency scrutiny and demand for program value-for-money advisory as the government seeks to frame structural bracket-creep revenue as compatible with cost-of-living relief. Housing (Victoria's homelessness model as a replicable template), infrastructure (Brisbane 2032 delivery pipeline, Snowy governance failure), and energy transition (Commonwealth grid and storage frameworks) reinforce a strong forward pipeline for delivery assurance, governance advisory, and program design work across the full PEPI portfolio.
